title: Shortcuts or Memorisation? Revisiting Data Corruption in Natural Language Understanding with Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.16843v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Pre-trained encoders fine-tuned on natural language inference (NLI) and other language understanding tasks keep much of their accuracy after the input is perturbed, e.g. by removing all nouns or shuffling the words. Does the same hold for large language models (LLMs), and if so, is it because they have seen the benchmarks during pre-training? In this paper we revisit these perturbation experiments with eight LLMs alongside fine-tuned encoders on GLUE and the three rounds of ANLI. Regardless of model size, every system that answers directly retains 36-72% of its above-chance performance without nouns on MNLI compared to only 14-29% on ANLI. Only a model that reasons before answering departs from this pattern. We also check contamination indicators (including exact $n$-gram counts in the public pre-training data of two of the models) and find no link between exposure and robustness. translated_title: 捷径还是记忆？利用大语言模型重新审视自然语言理解中的数据破坏
translated_abstract: 在自然语言推理（NLI）及其他语言理解任务上微调的预训练编码器，即使输入受到扰动（例如删除所有名词或打乱词序），仍能保持大部分准确率。大语言模型（LLM）是否也是如此？如果是，这是否是因为它们在预训练期间见过这些基准测试数据？本文使用八个大语言模型以及在GLUE和三轮ANLI上的微调编码器重新开展了这些扰动实验。无论模型规模大小，所有直接作答的系统在删除名词后的MNLI上仍保留了36-72%的超过随机水平的性能，而在ANLI上仅保留14-29%。只有在回答前先进行推理的模型才脱离了这一模式。我们还检查了数据污染指标（包括在两个模型的公开预训练数据中统计精确的n-gram出现次数），发现数据暴露与鲁棒性之间并无关联。我们最有力的证据来自368个新的、经人工验证的……
tldr: 该研究通过对八个大语言模型在GLUE和ANLI上的系统性扰动实验证明，语言模型面对数据破坏的鲁棒性来源于对捷径特征的利用而非对预训练数据的记忆，且只有在作答前先进行推理的模型才能摆脱这种捷径依赖模式。
en_tdlr: Revisiting perturbation experiments with eight LLMs on GLUE and ANLI, this paper demonstrates that models' robustness to data corruption stems from shortcut exploitation rather than memorisation of pre-training data, and only models that reason before answering escape this shortcut-reliance pattern.
